A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NewtonGen work. The main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation comparisons in Table 1, NND ablations in Table 2, prediction analyses in Appendix C and generated examples in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds background-consistency and motion-smoothness scores, plus an experiment training NND on real falling videos in Section 5.3.

M1.justification: The nine-dimensional state, linear ODE plus residual MLP, training loss, Algorithm 1 and optical-flow-conditioned generation pipeline remain unchanged. Appendix F corrects 'not train-free' to 'training-free,' consistent with the inference-only conditioning already described in v1; no new procedure is established.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 extends training-data coverage from physics-clean simulations to real, motion-blurred falling videos selected from PISABench, followed by generation in new scenes. This introduces a materially different data domain, although the extension is limited to falling motion. The original twelve motion categories remain.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain Sora, Veo3, CogVideoX-5B, Wan2.2 and the method cited as Xue et al. (2025). 'PhysT2V' is corrected to 'PhyT2V,' rather than replaced by another baseline. VBench supplies metrics, not an additional comparator.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 add VBench background consistency and motion smoothness throughout the main comparison, substantially broadening evaluation beyond physical invariance. Section 5.3 adds a real-video training-and-generation experiment. The original NND training budget, prompt protocol and Appendix D.1 PIS preprocessing remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and new Figure 5 add a focused feasibility analysis of learning falling dynamics from real videos containing motion blur, showing extracted masks, predicted dynamics and generated scenes. The MLP and training-data-scale ablations and Appendix C prediction analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly reports standard deviations across videos throughout the comparison, replacing central-score-only reporting. This does not establish additional independent runs: the fixed-seed statement and Appendix D.1 median-over-twelve-videos aggregation remain. Some new PIS deviations conflict with the stated bounded metric, creating a reporting problem.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds BC/MS results for every method and motion, while all original PIS central values and Table 2 ablation values remain identical. For example, new 3D-motion BC scores favor Wan2.2 (0.9772) over NewtonGen (0.9672). Real-video-trained NewtonGen additionally reports PIS-vx 0.8485 and PIS-ay 0.6008 under different training conditions.

T1.justification: The physical-state definition, autonomous dynamics assumptions, Equations 1–7 and mathematical content of Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The new prose problem definition and adoption of existing VBench metrics introduce no new formal derivation or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: physics-consistent, controllable generation through NND learned from limited physics-clean data. The additional experiments support these contributions without materially redefining their claimed scope.

C2.justification: The new real-video discussion interprets learning despite motion blur as feasible, while emphasizing lower data quality, collection effort and the cost advantages of simulation. The existing limitations concerning continuous dynamics and multi-object interactions remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 specifies mask centroids, axes, orientation and inter-frame velocity extraction more explicitly, and Appendix F clarifies training-free second-stage inference. The abstract changes the reported data/code status from future release to available at the existing repository target; Appendix A–B add project-page and repository access directions. Actual external availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to VBench for the new metrics and Likephys for the motivation concerning physical understanding. The related-work taxonomy, principal comparisons with earlier approaches and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short Problem Definition, clarifies several method descriptions, corrects terminology and removes author email addresses. The limitations paragraph moves into the conclusion, and the Appendix D.2 heading and pointer are removed while Table 3 remains. These are localized edits rather than a narrative overhaul.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains metric subrows and parenthesized deviations, and Figure 5 adds the real-video experiment. Figure 4 moves, the opening teaser is resized, and existing appendix comparisons are re-rendered at higher resolution and renumbered. The framework diagram, prediction plots and original visual examples retain their content.

improvement.justification: The real-video feasibility study, broader quality metrics and clearer technical documentation strengthen validation and explanation. However, new Table 1 uncertainty reporting introduces an unresolved inconsistency: Sora's parabolic-with-rotation PIS-ay has a stated standard deviation of 2.581 although Equation 7 bounds PIS in [0,1]. The PDFs do not clarify whether the labels or calculations are wrong. The useful additions and uncertain severity of this central reporting defect prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
